examples.text: The disaster shocked the world.

glosses: To give an electric shock to.
To subject to a shock wave or violent impact.

examples.text: Ammonium nitrate can detonate if severely shocked.

glosses: To meet with a shock; to collide in a violent encounter.

examples.text: They saw the moment approach when the two parties would shock together.

glosses: To add a chemical to (a swimming pool) to moderate the chlorine levels.

To deform the crystal structure of a stone by the application of extremely high pressure at moderate temperature, as produced only by hypervelocity impact events, lightning strikes, and nuclear explosions.

examples.text: It takes more than two gigapascals (two billion pascals) of pressure to shock quartz in this manner (for comparison, the atmosphere at sea level exerts a little over 100,000 pascals of pressure).

glosses: An arrangement of sheaves for drying; a stook.

examples.text: Cause it on shocks to be by and by set.

glosses: A lot consisting of sixty pieces; a term applied in some Baltic ports to loose goods.
A tuft or bunch of something, such as hair or grass.

examples.text: His head boasted a shock of sandy hair.
Every now and then I’m startled at how good-looking John is, but he glared at me from under the shock of hair that fell across his brow and scared me a little.
On day three I pointed at the edge of an intricate pentagram peeking above her shock of oily black hair.

glosses: A small dog with long shaggy hair, especially a poodle or spitz; a shaggy lapdog.

examples.text: When I read of witty persons, I could not figure them but like the little shock. (translating the German Spitz)

glosses: To collect, or make up, into a shock or shocks; to stook.
